newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Cetes rates end lower despite Lozano news.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Cetes rates end lower despite Lozano news.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down 70 basis points at 27.80 percent on Monday on local and international demand.

News just a few minutes before the close of trade that Attorney General Antonio Lozano had been fired came too late to affect the market, but cast a shadow on the outlook for interest rates, dealers said.
The news was likely to pressure rates on Tuesday and check an expected fall in primary rates later in the day.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 40 basis points at 29.10 basis points.
Banco de Mexico injected 7.385 billion pesos by auctioning five credits, which it assigned at between 29.01 percent and 29.45 percent.
Credit maturities for Tuesday were estimated at 8.166 billion pesos.
